rows.title: Existence of regular open and closed XOR-magic graphs of power-of-two order
rows.record_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $d$ be a degree. An **open XOR-magic graph** and a **closed XOR-magic graph** are graphs admitting, respectively, an open or closed XOR-magic labeling. The graphs below are required to have order $2^n$.

For each degree

$$
d\in\{5,7,\ldots,2^n-7,2^n-5\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular open XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$. For each degree

$$
d\in\{4,6,\ldots,2^n-6,2^n-4\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular closed XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$.

**Existence conjecture.** For every permitted degree $d$ in the two displayed sets, the corresponding regular open or closed XOR-magic graph exists. This would complete the existence picture apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result and extend the constructions known for order $16$ and order $8$ to every order that is a power of two.
rows.source: Sylwia Cichacz, Hubert Grochowski and Rita Zuazua, “Open XOR-magic odd graphs and closed XOR-magic even graphs”, arXiv:2512.19278 (2025).
rows.what_was_proved: For every n >= 4 and every odd d with 5 <= d <= 2^n-5 there is a connected d-regular open XOR-magic graph of order 2^n, and for every even d with 4 <= d <= 2^n-6 a connected d-regular closed one. This proves the Cichacz-Grochowski-Zuazua existence conjecture for every degree not excluded by the known nonexistence result (Batal; source Prop. 24), which is the scope the MathDB record states; the printed closed endpoint 2^n-4 is impossible by that known result, so the conjecture as literally printed is false there (no credit claimed for that correction).

rows.title: Cardoso–Luz conjecture on adverse graphs
rows.record_statement:
An **adverse graph** is a graph $H$ without isolated vertices such that $upsilon(H)$ and $lambda_{min}(H)$ are integers, and, for every vertex $i\in V(H)$,

$$
\upsilon(H-N_H(i))=\upsilon(H),\qquad \lambda_{min}(H-N_H(i))=\lambda_{min}(H).
$$

Here $upsilon(H)$ is the optimal value of the quadratic stability-number bound and $lambda_{min}(H)$ is the least eigenvalue of $H$. A graph is a **$\mathcal{Q}$-graph** when it belongs to the class $\mathcal{Q}$ defined in the paper.

**Cardoso–Luz conjecture.** All adverse graphs are $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.

Computational tests with adverse graphs supported the conjecture, but it remains open. Its resolution would clarify the polynomial-time recognition of $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.
rows.source: Domingos M. Cardoso, “A survey on graphs with convex quadratic stability number”, arXiv:1811.05516 (2018).
rows.what_was_proved: The cyclic Latin-square graph on the 36 cells of the order-six addition table has no isolated vertices, has least adjacency eigenvalue −3 and quadratic stability bound 6, and both values persist after deletion of the open neighborhood of each vertex. Its stability number is 5, so it is an adverse graph outside the class where the quadratic bound equals the stability number.

rows.title: The prime-modulus conjecture for progression-free digit sets
rows.record_statement:
Let $p\geq 13$ be a prime with $p\equiv 1\bmod 4$, and let $n$ be an integer divisible by $(p+3)/2$. For a digit set $D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p$, write $S(D,n)$ for the set of vectors in $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ in which every digit of $D$ occurs the same number of times. Define

$$
D=\left\{0,1,\ldots,\frac{p-1}{2},\frac{p+3}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Prime-modulus progression-free-set conjecture.** The set $S(D,n)$ does not contain any arithmetic progression of length $4$.

This conjecture extends the progression-free constructions for odd progression lengths to a case not covered by the stated theorem, motivated by computations with small primes. Its status is unresolved in the source.
rows.source: Christian Elsholtz, Benjamin Klahn and Gabriel F. Lipnik, “Large Subsets of Z_m^n without Arithmetic Progressions”, arXiv:2211.02588 (2022).
rows.what_was_proved: For every natural modulus p≥13 congruent to 1 modulo 4 and every natural n, any four vectors in (ℤ/pℤ)ⁿ with both coordinatewise second differences zero are equal if each uses only digits 0 through (p−1)/2 and (p+3)/2, each exactly n/((p+3)/2) times. In particular, the specified prime-modulus sets contain no four-term arithmetic progression of nonzero step.

rows.title: Nonexistence conjecture for cubic 8-circulant nut graphs
rows.record_statement: A **cubic $8$-circulant nut graph** is a cubic nut graph admitting an $8$-circulant structure. **Nonexistence conjecture for cubic $8$-circulant nut graphs.** There exists no cubic $8$-circulant nut graph. This is the only unresolved case in the cubic $\ell$-circulant nut graph existence problem; computational results suggest that such graphs might not exist, but no proof is given here.
rows.source: Nino Bašić and Ivan Damnjanović, “On cubic polycirculant nut graphs”, arXiv:2411.16904 (2024).
rows.what_was_proved: No finite simple cubic graph whose real adjacency kernel is one-dimensional and contains a vector nonzero at every vertex admits an automorphism with exactly eight orbits of equal size. This rules out a cubic eight-circulant nut graph at every order.

rows.title: Contact-order distance conjecture for colored graph representations
rows.record_statement: Let $G$ be a graph whose vertices are colored with $z$ and $w$, and let $i$ be a vertex from which the representation is computed. The **contact order** is the order describing how the associated level curves approach one another near a boundary singularity. **Contact-order distance conjecture.** The contact order of the representation computed from vertex $i$ is twice the path distance from $i$ to the closest vertex colored $w$. The source reports computational evidence for this extension, but does not state a proof or resolution.
rows.source: Lily Adlin, Giovani Thai, Samuel Tiscareno and Ryan Tully-Doyle, “Cauchy Transforms of Colored Graphs in Two Variables”, arXiv:2410.10695 (2025).
rows.what_was_proved: Conjecture 6.1 of Adlin-Thai-Tiscareno-Tully-Doyle (arXiv:2410.10695) is false: for the 5-vertex graph with edges 01, 02, 03, 13, 24, 34, root 0 and w-coloured vertices 1 and 2, the nearest w-vertex is at distance 1 but the contact order at the singularity (inf,0) is 6, in the sense of Bickel-Pascoe-Sola (Definition 2.5: maximum branch order of the zero set of the reduced numerator after the Cayley transform), as certified in Lean; the level-curve branches there have orders 6 and 2.

rows.title: Uniqueness conjecture for power domination reconfiguration graphs of complete bipartite graphs
rows.record_statement: Let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with part sizes $s$ and $t$, and let $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ denote its power domination reconfiguration graph under token addition/removal reconfiguration. **Uniqueness conjecture.** $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ is unique if and only if $s\ne 2$ and $t\ne 2$. This is supported by the uniqueness results for $K_{1,t}$ with $t\ge 3$ and $K_{3,3}$, together with Sage computations for $s\in\{3,4\}$ and $t\in\{3,4,5\}$; the conjecture proposes the complete characterization, including the cases not covered by those results.
rows.source: Beth Bjorkman, Chassidy Bozeman, Daniela Ferrero, Mary Flagg, Cheryl Grood, Leslie Hogben, Bonnie Jacob and Carolyn Reinhart, “Power domination reconfiguration”, arXiv:2201.01798 (2022).
rows.what_was_proved: For every pair of positive integers s,t, the power-domination TAR reconfiguration graph of K_{s,t} determines K_{s,t} up to isomorphism among finite simple graphs without isolated vertices exactly when neither s nor t equals two. The reconfiguration graph uses power-dominating vertex sets joined when their symmetric difference has size one.

rows.title: Conjecture on recurrent component cardinalities in sinkless rotor networks
rows.record_statement:
Let $C_n$ be the bidirected cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i}$ denote the unique recurrent component of level $m$ and weight $i\in\mathbb{Z}_n$. Write $r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i})$ for the number of recurrent configurations in this component.

**Recurrent-component cardinality conjecture.** For $n\geq 3$, $m\geq 1$, and $i,j\in\mathbb{Z}_n$, one has

$$
r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i})=r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,j})
$$

whenever

$$
\gcd(n,m,i)=\gcd(n,m,j).
$$

The conjecture refines the observed near equality of recurrent-component sizes in sinkless rotor networks on bidirected cycles. It is supported by data for small values of $m$ and $n$, but the supplied source does not state a resolution.
rows.source: Swee Hong Chan and Lionel Levine, “Abelian networks IV. Dynamics of nonhalting networks”, arXiv:1804.03322 (2020).
rows.what_was_proved: For every n≥3, m≥1 and i,j in ℤ/nℤ with gcd(n,m,i)=gcd(n,m,j), the bidirected-cycle rotor network has equally many recurrent natural configurations in the components of level m and weights i and j. Lean also shows there is a unique component with a recurrent natural representative of each specified level and weight and that the canonical component has a diverse legal walk.

rows.title: The 2-adic valuation conjecture for even-colored 2-ary partition functions
rows.record_statement:
Let $c_m(n)$ denote the $m$-colored binary partition function, and let $
u_2$ be the 2-adic valuation. For positive integers $k,n$ and nonnegative integers $k$ as specified below, consider the differences of the values of $c_m$. **2-adic valuation conjecture.** For $kin\mathbb{N}_{+}$ and each $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{2k}(4n)-c_{2k}(n))=\nu_{2}(n)+2\nu_{2}(k)+3.
$$
 Moreover, for $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+1}(4n)-c_{4k+1}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+3,
$$
 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+3}(4n)-c_{4k+3}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+6.
$$
 In each case, equality holds for infinitely many $n\in\mathbb{N}$. These predictions are motivated by known sharp congruences for the ordinary binary partition function and numerical computations for $m\leq10$ and $n\leq10^5$; their general validity remains open.
rows.source: Maciej Ulas and Błażej Żmija, “On p-adic valuations of certain m colored p-ary partition functions”, arXiv:1904.03398 (2019).
rows.what_was_proved: For every positive n the differences c_m(4n)−c_m(n), using 2m colors for parts of size one and m for each other binary part size, are nonzero and have 2-adic valuation ν₂(n)+2ν₂(k)+3 for m=2k≥2, at least ν₂(n)+3 for m≡1 mod 4, and at least ν₂(n)+6 for m≡3 mod 4. The odd bounds are attained for odd n when m≡1 mod 4 or m≡3,7 mod 16, and for n≡2 mod 4 when m≡11 mod 16, whereas m≡15 mod 16 always gives at least ν₂(n)+7, refuting the per-color infinite-equality reading and proving the some-color reading.

rows.title: Even-arity complete full tree local antimagic chromatic number conjecture
rows.record_statement:
Let $T$ be a complete full $t$-ary tree, meaning a rooted tree in which every nonleaf has exactly $t$ children and all leaves have the same depth. Let $l$ be the number of leaves and let $\chi_{la}(T)$ be the local antimagic chromatic number. **Even-arity complete full tree conjecture.** For every even integer $t\geq2$,

$$
\chi_{la}(T)=l+1.
$$

The paper explicitly states this conjecture as open; it would sharpen the established upper bound $\chi_{la}(T)\leq l+2$, while the equality is proved in the paper for odd $t$.
rows.source: Martin Bača, Andrea Semaničová-Feňovčíková, Ruei-Ting Lai and Tao-Ming Wang, “On local antimagic vertex coloring for complete full t-ary trees”, arXiv:2204.04479 (2022).
rows.what_was_proved: Every finite complete full t-ary tree of common leaf depth n ≥ 1 with even t ≥ 2 has local antimagic chromatic number equal to one plus its number of degree-one vertices, and a labelling attains that minimum. Here a labelling is a bijection from the edges to 1 through the edge count with unequal incident-label sums across each edge, and the standard tree model has minimum tⁿ+1.

rows.title: Intermediate-value conjecture for orientable total domination numbers
rows.record_statement:
Let $G\in\mathcal{C}$ be a graph, and let ${\rm dom}_t(G)$ and ${\rm DOM}_t(G)$ denote its lower and upper orientable total domination numbers. For an orientation $f$ of $G$, write $G_f$ for the resulting oriented graph and $\gamma_t(G_f)$ for its total domination number. **Intermediate-value conjecture.** For every integer $c$ satisfying

$$
{\rm dom}_t(G)\leq c\leq {\rm DOM}_t(G),
$$

there exists an orientation $f$ of $G$ such that

$$
\gamma_t(G_f)=c.
$$

This extends the corresponding result known for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs. The source attributes the conjecture to the authors of the cited earlier work, and no resolution is given here.
rows.source: Sarah E. Anderson, Tanja Dravec, Daniel Johnston and Kirsti Kuenzel, “Orientable total domination in graphs”, arXiv:2311.16307 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: For every finite graph admitting an orientation of positive indegree at each vertex, every integer between the minimum and maximum attained total domination numbers is itself attained by such an orientation. Total domination requires each vertex, including each set member, to have an in-neighbour in the set.
